[Spoiler=expansion post]After​‍​‌‍​‍‌​‍​‌‍​‍‌ weeks of careful naval scouting and diplomay work, Valddera reached out to a big, island, half of it was unoccupied from any nation, as that island was of great strategic and economic interest. The journey was planned to show restraint, communication, and stability rather than use of force. Valdderan ships arrived at the harbors of the towns, where envoys greeted the local councils and community leaders. The island government was a complex but well-organized system. Different councils controlled their areas and worked together on trade, law, and defense issues. Despite the internal rivalries among the councils, they had certain vulnerabilities in common, such as being exposed to piracy, illegal trafficking, and foreign exploitation. Valdderan diplomats identified these issues and thus presented their offer, saying that the island's being left alone made it susceptible to be dominated by more powerful but less scrupulous forces. The talks proceeded slowly through public meetings, ceremonial councils, and secret discussions. Valdvera assured the local authorities of her respect to their governance, religion, and cultural institutes and offered security at sea, money for infrastructure, and access to the world trade network in exchange for some supervision. Most importantly, Valdvera gave the promise that there would be no interference in choosing the internal leadership and in domestic law. This promise enabled the local leaders to talk freely as they did not have to show that they gave up their sovereignty. The treaty thus resulting and signed on board a Valdderan flagship, officially made the island a protectorate with a status of self-governing. As per the agreement, Valddera took over the responsibility of foreign relations, the external security, and the management of natural resources. The island councils had the freedom to make decisions about internal law, taxation, education, and cultural matters. The two sides set up joint councils to monitor the treaty implementation and solve any issues arising from it, thereby preventing one-sided dominance. After the signing, Valddera sent a few civilian engineers, administrators, and security advisors. The upgrade of the island's infrastructure became the main focus. The harbors were revamped for bigger boats, thus facilitating both trade and patrol missions. Roads and transport links were built to connect the towns and villages and thus cut the isolation. Communication means were enhanced to make administrative coordination more efficient and at the same time, local authority structures were preserved. The collaborative geological studies later on revealed they had vast reserves of uranium accompanied by rare metals and industrial minerals. Valdvera intentionally postponed the mining activities until all the environmental and social impact assessment reports were ready. Mining operations were set up as joint ventures, and revenue-sharing arrangements were formalized in the legislation. A considerable share of the gains was allocated to pump priming the commnity, among other things, healthcare facilities, education programs and housing. All mining activities were regulated by strict safety and environmental standards. Valdderan equipment minimized pollution risks and made sure the land was returned to its original state after industrial use. The local people had their representatives who were directly involved in the supervision committees, thus ensuring their accountability and long-term sustainability. The uranium consignments were delivered to their destination under the watch of the security forces who ensured safety against robbery and foreign intervention while letting the civilian life go on as usual. The process of cultural merging was carried out with caution. The bilingual education programs helped in raising the general literacy level and the technical skills while the native language and the local history were also taught. The religious institutions were given the complete freedom to carry on their work and the traditional festivals were granted legal protection. The academic and artistic exchange programs helped mutual understanding, leading to cultural blending without the forced assimilation. The protectorate was split into different areas each governed by councils that operated under a central assembly. The Valdderan officials were there only as advisers on the matters of budgeting, infrastructure planning, and treaty obligations and they didn't have any direct authority over the internal legislation. The legal systems were a mix of customary law and standardized protections that were put in place to ensure fairness, stability, and minority rights. The security strategy was mainly about deterrence from the enemy side rather than an occupation of the area. The Valddera kept only a few professional units at the ports and some strategic installations, while the local forces were in charge of the internal security and maintaining the law and order among the civilians. The joint training programs were there to enhance the skills, coordination, disaster response, and territorial defense. The surveillance and patrol networks were the eyes and ears in the waters that surrounded them and their presence acted as a deterrent to those who were into illegal activities and those who wanted to enter the territory unnoticed. With the efforts of the protectorate, there was sustained economic growth. Agriculture and fisheries were developed with the help of regulated frameworks, while processing plants made it possible for the locals to refine the raw materials that were from their own region. The trade routes that were established connected the island to the regional markets, thus the islanders were able to reduce their dependence and at the same time increase their resilience. The transparent taxation and the visible public investment were the two main things that strengthened the trust in governance. The social relations evolved gradually. The trade, education, and migration were the main factors that led to personal and professional ties between the Valdderans and the islanders. The intermarriage and the shared institutions produced the generation that was bilingual in both traditions and this was the foundation for the long-term stability and loyalty. From a strategic point of view, the island was a great asset for Valddera in terms of naval reach, energy security, and diplomatic influence. The island's ports were the base for the maritime presence along the important routes, while the resource flows were the fuel for the industrial capacity. The international reactions were like a spectrum ranging from the cautious approval to the quiet concern, but still, there was not much criticism coming from outside thanks to Valddera's transparency and self-restraint. The long-term planning rested on two main points, sustainability and gradual self-sufficiency. The investments in renewable energy were the reason why the island was not dependent on uranium in the future, while the local governance leadership development programs were preparing them for the greater autonomy. Valddera saw themsleves as the stabilizing guarantor not the permanent ruler, hence, they were ensuring their influence through legitimacy and not through force. Valddera managed to create an overseas protectorate through the judicious use of power. by respecting authority, cooperating with the locals, keeping an eye on them and balancing all these elements against each other that could work not only as a senior partner but also as a genuine one, thereby, embedding their influence through consent, stability and shared prosperity. When things got secure and stable, Valddera declared the name of the island the land of Shymetau, as that what was usually called by the locals.[/spoiler]
